pages.title: Ruins and camps
text: The tribes left more behind than halls and drum circles. Every land of the March has its own remains, most of them with a chest worth opening, and a few guarded by what still walks there.

The Old Gate Ruin and the Crystal Grotto keep their best chests behind **Hollow Sentinels**, and the Ash Tomb behind spawners of **Ashbound** and **Cinder Imps**. Those chests can hold a **Resonant Core** or **Loom Thread**.

pages.title: Camps and villages
text: Every tribe keeps a camp in each band of the March, built from that band's own wood and ground: frostpine and snow on the frozen rim, thornfir and needle loam in the cold taigas, drumpalm on the savannas, sunbark and salt in the hot lands. The Pad-keepers hold the meadows and wolds, the Grit-singers the peaks and mesas, the Rootbinders the deep woods, the Edge-walkers the taigas, the Drumhearts the dry and burning ground, the Pattern-weavers the open steppes, the Colony-keepers the flowering lands, the Seal-carvers the dark woods and the Loom-stitchers the strange, lit country.

**Villages** stand in every band too: a plaza with the tribe's hearth, fire, totem, well and loom, its four Kin, and the voice's own generator humming; streets of the band's stone leading to huts, longhouses, a workshop with an Echo Shatter and a Song Bench, a granary of the band's crop, a shrine, a watchtower, a pen of the band's grazers and a flower garden. A village's hearth takes offerings like a camp's.

pages.title: Pieces of the old world
text: Over the peaks and the high ground, and over many a Weeping Colossus, **floating mountains of the old world** hang in the sky: tall crags of March rock, wide at the crown and tapering to a point below, their faces banded and mossy, turf and trees on top, a broken ring of bricks with a chest in it, vines down every side and a waterfall pouring off the rim. They hang in clusters at different heights, bridged by giant vines, small rocks drifting about them.

A cluster is held to the ground by **giant roots of willow wood**, sheathed in leaves and hung with curtains of willow strands that run the whole way down. The strands are climbable: take hold at the foot of a root and climb to the sky. Over a colossus the roots end in its crown, so the tree is the ladder.

pages.title: The Steppe and the Highlands
text: - **Wayfarer's Shrine**: a roofed roadside shrine on an old path, with an offering chest.
- **Grazing Stones**: a ring of standing stones around a salt-lick.
- **Abandoned Waystation**: a ruined relay post, one mast still standing.
- **Fallen Drum Tower**: a broken tower; its great drum lies in the grass.
- **Watchfire Beacon**: a stone tower on a knoll with its signal fire still lit.
- **Echo Quarry**: a terraced pit with March ores in its walls and a crane at the rim.
- **Storm Altar**: a tuff altar under a lightning rod.
- **Seal-carver's Retreat**: rooms cut into a crag, with a workshop and a loft.
- **Old Gate Ruin**: a half-buried Way Gate over a guarded hall and a barred vault.

pages.title: The Snow Fields and the Ember Wastes
text: - **Frozen Longhall**, **Ice Cairn**, **Hunter's Lodge** and **Aurora Watch** in the snow.
- **Ember Forge**, **Cinder Spire** and **Slag Ring** in the ash, and the **Remnant Den** where survivors held out.
- **Ash Tomb**: a buried tomb under the Wastes, guarded, and worth the risk.

pages.title: The Crystal Fields and the Reed Fen
text: - **Shattered Observatory**: a star-chart terrace under a broken dome.
- **Resonance Obelisk**: a crystal-capped obelisk over a hidden vault.
- **Loom Ruin**: a fallen great loom, cloth still hanging.
- **Crystal Grotto**: a spiral stair down to a geode cave and a vault behind an iron door.
- **Stilt Village**, **Sunken Shrine**, **Reed Weir** and **Bog Barrow** in the fen.
- **Spirit Well**: a roofed well ringed with blooms, its offering chest at the bottom of the water.
